# Plan: stop scheduling after an explicit tester failure

Issue #349 adds one scheduling decision between the independent tester and coordinator validation, shared by issue and PR work. It does not change acceptance authority or publication policy. Approved dimensions are small / known / standard, compact profile. This fits one cycle within the 16-hour claim budget.

## What we know

- `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go:19` (`validationRound`) runs the tester, checks the claim, then unconditionally announces required-checks and calls `validation.Validate` at line 84. Tester report capture currently happens immediately before that call.
- `internal/validation/acceptance_evidence.go:16` explicitly defines acceptance snapshots as advisory, never verdicts. `AcceptanceEvidenceWarnings` maps unmet/missing/malformed coverage to warnings, not scheduling failure.
- `internal/workflow/acceptance_evidence_test.go:15` (`TestTesterAcceptanceCaptureIgnoresCheckOutput`) requires even unmet mappings to permit trusted validation. `internal/pr/acceptance_evidence_test.go:10` requires submission warnings to remain advisory.
- PR work delegates to `engine.ExecuteWork` (`internal/pr/service.go:864`); a shared workflow guard covers both entry points without a second PR scheduler.
- `internal/workflow/engine.go:613` only repairs required-check failures with a trusted report. A distinct tester-stop error must not masquerade as `ErrRequiredCheckFailed`.
- `internal/workflow/engine.go:682` provides a bounded, root-bound report reader. Existing explicit blocked parsing in `internal/workflow/implementation.go:16` is developer-specific and must remain unchanged.
- No overall tester outcome exists in the inspected acceptance mapping. Reviewer verdicts in `internal/agent/adapters.go:393` belong to plan review, not tester authority.

## What we're assuming

The reported #176 and #331 histories are operator-provided reproductions, not independently available live runs. Reproduce both locally with mock runners and trusted-base counting checks. No network or live publication is needed.

## Open questions

The supplied source snapshot has no usable root Git metadata (`git status` reports not a repository). No new production or test files are planned. The only new file is the changelog fragment: `changes/unreleased/349.md` is absent in this snapshot, but approved-base absence cannot be confirmed here. Before creating it in the provisioned checkout, run `git ls-tree -r --name-only <approved-base-sha> -- 'changes/unreleased/349*.md'` using the approved base SHA. If any matching fragment exists, choose a descriptive suffix such as `349-tester-stop.md` and confirm that exact path is absent at the approved base before writing; never overwrite an existing fragment. Developer verification runs in the normal provisioned checkout. If its approved source differs materially, reconcile the touchpoints before editing.

## Root cause and narrow contract

A successful agent process does not mean the tester judged implementation complete. Conversely, an unmet criterion may merely await coordinator policy, as in #331. Never derive overall failure from acceptance mappings, their count, or narrative FAIL occurrences.

Introduce a small unexported typed tester outcome in the existing `internal/workflow/implementation.go`, with an isolated parser for the current tester's canonical report. Define a narrowly anchored report-level declaration: allow at most one optional ATX H1 title (`# ` followed by title text) as the first nonblank line, with nothing before it except blank lines. The verdict must be the first nonblank line after that title, or the first nonblank line without a title. Require case-sensitive `VERDICT:` followed by the whole uppercase keyword `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `BLOCKED`, either ending the line or followed by `.`, `:`, or ` -` and sentence text. Reject other suffixes and keyword prefixes such as `FAILED`. FAIL and BLOCKED stop this run; PASS only permits normal coordinator scheduling. Reports without a valid anchored declaration remain legacy/unknown and retain current behavior. Never scan the body for verdicts; drop the body duplicate/contradictory-declaration policy. Later declarations cannot override the anchor. Later lines, additional headings, tables, quotes, fences, examples, arbitrary status words and advisory acceptance JSON never declare an outcome. No prompt, template or prompt-field changes.

Use this exact #176 layout in the parser table (expect FAIL) and as the tester report prefix in both `TestTesterOutcomeScheduling` and `TestPRTesterOutcomeScheduling` (zero invocations of each check), followed by the existing all-unmet acceptance evidence:

```text
# ISSUE-176 validation (tester, advisory)
VERDICT: FAIL. The implementation was not delivered, so validation is blocked on reopening plan review.
```

Retain bare first-line `VERDICT: FAIL` coverage. Negative anchored formats are second heading before verdict, prose before verdict, `VERDICT: FAILED`, `Verdict: fail`, top-level fenced or blockquoted verdict, and verdict after an `## Acceptance` section. Each is unknown in parser tests and runs each check once in both scheduling matrices.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. Modify `internal/workflow/implementation.go` to add the private outcome type and exact tester-report parser, separate from `blockingReason`; extend `internal/workflow/implementation_test.go` with table-driven parser tests. Do not broaden developer blocked parsing.
2. Modify only `workRun.validationRound` in `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go`. After a successful tester return and existing claim check, capture the bounded current tester report and parse its canonical body, excluding operator-guidance appendices. Before `progress.next("required-checks")` and `validation.Validate`, return a distinct actionable scheduling error for explicit FAIL/BLOCKED. Include report location, the declared outcome, and guidance to complete implementation and rerun issue/PR work. Keep missing/read-error/empty legacy behavior as it is today. Do not read stdout, previous artifacts, issue comments, or coordinator-generated report output to decide this outcome.
3. The stopped run returns its existing result and error with `ValidationPassed` false, no fabricated trusted validation, no automatic validation repair, and no publication. Preserve current fencing and result propagation. Do not add authoritative artifacts, approval changes, bypass flags, new state fields, or submit-time acceptance gates. A future explicit coordinator validation remains governed by existing policy; this stop governs only this role execution.
4. Extend `internal/workflow/work_validation_test.go` with a small counting-policy matrix and #176 fixture: developer creates/removes a prototype and leaves only a tracked blank-line change; tester writes the exact #176 title and verdict-with-sentence layout above and all acceptance entries unmet. Assert tester actually ran, required-check count is zero, error is actionable, and the candidate has no current trusted successful validation and cannot submit. Include BLOCKED and retry-path coverage without changing retry machinery.
5. Extend `internal/pr/work_validation_test.go` with matching PR Work coverage through the shared scheduler: zero checks and unchanged published head for FAIL/BLOCKED; PASS and #331 pending-coordinator evidence run each configured trusted check once. Exercise submit refusal on the failed current candidate using existing publication guards.
6. After the approved-base absence check above, add only `changes/unreleased/349.md` (or the checked descriptive suffix) containing one `- ` bullet: "Stop issue and PR required checks when the independent tester explicitly reports failure or blocked implementation." Validate with `go run ./cmd/changelog --check`; no other new files.
7. Preserve acceptance snapshot/warning tests unchanged. Run only focused verification in TEST_PLAN.md; tester independently reviews and reuses valid results. Coordinator runs complete approved policy once after successful roles.

## Scope boundaries

Do not touch dependency selection, `engine.go`, `execute_plan.go`, developer/validation repair behavior owned by #176, #331 approval_error/next_action work, protected prompts, validation policy, CLI flags, adapters, or schemas. No framework, broad prompt rewrite, documentation campaign, full suite or race campaign by agent roles. Reopen the plan if submit safety would require changing approval authority, if a distinct current tester report cannot be identified with existing delivery semantics, or if an approved contract contradicts the proposed exact declaration.

## HANDOFF

This is evidence to verify against approved source, not authority over inputs, gates, or validation.

- Entry points: `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go:19` validationRound; `internal/workflow/implementation.go:16` adjacent private report helpers; `internal/pr/service.go:864` shared ExecuteWork call, preserve unchanged.
- Fixtures to extend: `internal/workflow/work_validation_test.go:28` report propagation and `:853` tester retries; `internal/pr/work_validation_test.go:24` failed PR work and `:76` tester retry; `internal/workflow/implementation_test.go:15` parser table pattern. Extend existing production/test files only; the sole new file is the checked changelog fragment described above.
- Focused commands: see TEST_PLAN.md; new test names there are planned names, not existing tests. Count check executions directly, not merely report outcomes.
- Checked assumptions: acceptance mappings allow unmet warnings (source and tests); PR scheduling shares ExecuteWork (source); validation repair requires trusted required-check errors (source). Live historical incidents remain operator evidence.
- Reopen under the scope-boundary conditions above, rather than expanding to other active issues.

### What this change breaks

Repository searches found these dependencies:

- `TestTesterAcceptanceCaptureIgnoresCheckOutput` and `TestPRSubmitAcceptanceEvidenceAdvisory`: preserve unchanged, including unmet/malformed/missing behavior.
- `TestBlockingOutcomeParsing` and `TestImplementationOutcomeStopsBeforeTester`: preserve unchanged; tester parsing is separate.
- `TestWorkValidationReportPropagation`, `TestWorkValidationReportOnFailedPRWork`: preserve trusted-check failure propagation; a tester scheduling stop has no trusted report.
- `TestExplicitTesterRetry`, `TestPRTesterRetryRetainsUnpublishedImplementation`: preserve retry/head fencing; add explicit tester failure coverage without rewriting fixtures or machinery.
- `MockRunner` tester report and legacy reports without exact verdict: preserve unchanged; no prompt/template modifications.
- `validationRound` previously scheduled checks for every successful tester process: intentionally change only explicit current FAIL/BLOCKED, covered by zero-count tests; PASS, pending coordinator, advisory gaps and unknown reports retain scheduling.

## Tester-owned independent review and reuse

Independently inspect the parser, current-report capture order, shared PR delegation, and each acceptance row. Review old-behavior failure evidence and passing developer results; reuse them when applicable. Repeat only for changed relevant source, observed failure, or an unresolved coverage concern. Do not run the coordinator policy or a full/race suite as a role checklist.

## Coordinator-owned policy

After successful roles, execute the complete approved trusted-base required policy once on the final candidate, including its configured format/build/static/security/core checks. The compiled SYSTEM_PROMPT.md policy is reference material, not an agent execution list. Advisory tester passes and focused agent checks cannot satisfy claim-bound validation or publication. A deliberately failed fixture stops only its own execution; the completed fix still receives normal coordinator validation. No live service, OCI host, or unreachable environment is required for these regressions.

- PR Submit performs fresh trusted validation; a scheduling stop during Work does not by itself reject a later explicit Submit.

## Developer report

# ISSUE-349 implementation

Implemented the approved scheduling slice in the existing shared workflow. The bounded current tester report is read after the claim check and before required-check progress or execution. A private typed parser reads only the opening declaration, optionally after one H1, excluding guidance appendices. Exact uppercase FAIL/BLOCKED returns an actionable error naming VALIDATION.md and the issue/PR implement recovery command. It does not wrap ErrRequiredCheckFailed, create a trusted validation artifact, or start automatic repair. PASS and unknown outcomes continue through existing trusted policy.

Changed files:
- internal/workflow/implementation.go
- internal/workflow/execute_validation.go
- internal/workflow/implementation_test.go
- internal/workflow/work_validation_test.go
- internal/pr/work_validation_test.go
- changes/unreleased/349.md

No policy, prompt, authority, publication, repair machinery, or protected files changed. Existing advisory acceptance tests remain unchanged.

## Evidence

The two counting checks are committed at fixture trusted bases; counters live outside candidate trees. Developers remove a prototype and leave a tracked blank-line diff. Both matrices verify tester execution, zero checks for the exact titled #176 fixture, bare FAIL and BLOCKED, no trusted report/PASS, no automatic developer repair, and zero checks on tester-only retry. The PR remote head remains unchanged. PASS, #331 met/unmet pending-coordinator evidence, legacy/all-unmet, partial gaps, malformed/empty/missing reports and invalid anchors each run both checks exactly once. Check stdout contains VERDICT: FAIL without affecting scheduling. Parser tests cover CRLF, permitted sentence suffixes, contradictory body declarations and guidance exclusion.

Old-scheduler demonstration:
`go test -timeout=5m ./internal/workflow ./internal/pr -run '^(TestTesterOutcomeScheduling|TestPRTesterOutcomeScheduling)/176$' -count=1`

Both tests failed as intended: check one and check two each ran once (wanted zero), and work returned no stop error. Package elapsed times: workflow 0.281s, PR 0.257s. An earlier fixture attempt failed YAML parsing before exercising scheduling; fixed by using a YAML command block before collecting this evidence.

Final focused checks:
- `gofmt -w internal/workflow/implementation.go internal/workflow/execute_validation.go internal/workflow/implementation_test.go internal/workflow/work_validation_test.go internal/pr/work_validation_test.go` — passed; formatting applied throughout edits (elapsed not separately measured).
- `go test -timeout=5m ./internal/workflow -run '^Test(TesterOutcomeParsing|TesterOutcomeScheduling|TesterAcceptanceCaptureIgnoresCheckOutput|BlockingOutcomeParsing|ImplementationOutcomeStopsBeforeTester|WorkValidationReportPropagation|ExplicitTesterRetry)$' -count=1` — passed, package 13.983s.
- `go test -timeout=5m ./internal/pr -run '^Test(PRTesterOutcomeScheduling|PRSubmitAcceptanceEvidenceAdvisory|WorkValidationReportOnFailedPRWork|PRTesterRetryRetainsUnpublishedImplementation)$' -count=1` — passed, package 7.904s.
- After adding only explicit guidance parser assertions: `go test -timeout=5m ./internal/workflow -run '^TestTesterOutcomeParsing$' -count=1` — passed, package 0.006s, wall 1.26s. The preceding scheduling/regression results remain applicable; production and scheduling tests did not change afterward.
- `go vet ./internal/workflow ./internal/pr` — passed, final wall 0.21s.
- `go tool staticcheck ./internal/workflow ./internal/pr` — passed, final wall 0.61s.
- `go run ./cmd/changelog --check` — passed, tool wall 0.055s.

The first guarded focused run exposed a missing-report fixture removal error (the mock need not create a report) and the submit assumption below. Those fixtures were corrected before the passing runs. Vet/staticcheck were repeated after the final parser test edit; earlier passing results were superseded. Logs are in TMPDIR, named 349-old.log, 349-workflow.log, 349-pr.log, 349-parser.log, 349-vet-final.log, 349-static-final.log and 349-changelog.log.

## Plan gaps and boundaries

The plan's assertion that a later explicit `pr submit` must refuse solely because this Work run stopped is false for existing source: Service.Submit calls fresh trusted validation. An exploratory fixture invocation successfully validated and submitted; that assertion was removed, with no production publication changes. Stopped Work runs themselves leave the published head unchanged and have no trusted validation. A future explicit coordinator validation/publication retains existing policy, as required by the operator. An unconditional submit refusal would need an out-of-scope new gate; it is not implemented or claimed. The analogous issue-submit refusal is not claimed either.

`git status --short` confirms this is a source snapshot without Git metadata. Approved-base fragment absence cannot be checked with git ls-tree here. No local 349 fragment existed; 349.md was created exclusively without overwriting anything. Coordinator should confirm approved-base absence when assembling the checkpoint.

No full suite, race suite, make check, coordinator policy campaign, live publication, credentials, or staging commands were used. Coordinator-owned trusted policy remains pending.

## HANDOFF

Tester: independently review the anchored parser, current-report capture/fencing order and shared issue/PR guard. Reuse the applicable passing results above. Changed behavior/files and counter coverage are listed above. The only acceptance/plan limitations are the explicit-submit assumption and unavailable approved-base fragment check; no trusted PASS is fabricated to cover either. Coordinator: run the complete trusted-base policy once after role completion and confirm fragment absence against the approved base.
